interview.name: Kira
interview.answer: It’s set for Saturday afternoon, at the repair drive location.

reflections: Bo is reliable and contributes practical support, but has limited transport capacity, so coordination should account for that.
Kira is organizing the repair drive by checking availability and resources, suggesting a logistics-focused role.
Sam is proactive and flexible, offering a broad range of help and waiting for specific direction.
Kira is acting as the organizer who repeatedly asks for precise confirmation before moving forward.
Sam and Quinn are both offering practical support, but Quinn is focused on outreach and volunteer/tool coordination while Sam covers hands-on repair help.
Cleo is tracking supplies closely and is already ready to share a concrete shortage list, which makes her a useful logistics contact.
Kira is coordinating practical details by repeatedly asking for confirmation on supplies, help needed, and timing.
Cleo is the main source for the repair-drive supply list and is only tracking a small, concrete set of shortages.
Quinn is actively recruiting support and has a clear outreach role in the repair drive.
Kira is consistently the coordinator, repeatedly asking for specific confirmations and narrowing the repair drive details.
Quinn is leading or organizing the repair drive and needs volunteers plus spare tools, with a clear Saturday afternoon timing.
The group is cooperative but some participants are overloaded or scattered, so concise, concrete requests help them respond effectively.
Kira consistently asks for concrete logistics and tries to keep coordination clear by confirming times, dates, and needed supplies.
Quinn, Eli, and Ira are responsive and solution-oriented, each offering partial information or help to move the repair drive forward.
The group seems to rely on iterative back-and-forth to fill gaps in planning, with Kira acting as a persistent coordinator.
